- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially when sentiment > 0.5 and recent prices are rising.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or when sentiment drops below 0.3 — model tends to overcorrect downward.
- Reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% when sentiment is low (e.g., < 0.2) or shows negative momentum.
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts after recent price peaks — model often overshoots by 2–5% in the first 5–7 days post-spike.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if 10-day average of true prices is significantly higher than recent forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model tends to lag — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days after sentiment peak.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 2–4% if sentiment is consistently below 0.5 over last 5 days — model overconfident in bearish signals.
